clue.text: Sour beer served by temp in centre

indicators.note: served by puts the beer after the piece from temp, which comes first
in centre asks for the middle letters of the word temp

parts.note: bitter is a type of British ale

explanation.surface: A drinker complains that the beer brought by a temporary barman tasted off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sour' looks like a description of the beer but it is a verb, the definition. Bitter is a British pale ale.
explanation.definitionFit: To sour someone is to make them resentful, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Succeed in exam? I don't know

definitions.meaning: to get through a test successfully
what a quiz contestant says to decline a question

explanation.surface: A student asked about exam success shrugs and admits ignorance.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting through an exam and declining a quiz question are both expressed by the same one-word verb or interjection.

clue.text: Minstrel booed playing instrument

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of minstrel booed are performed in a new order

explanation.surface: A wandering musician is jeered while performing on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' signals an anagram of MINSTREL BOOED.
explanation.definitionFit: This brass instrument with a sliding tube is an example of a musical instrument.

clue.text: Miss mostly seen round copper's place

indicators.note: seen round means the shortened word wraps around the copper symbol
mostly means the word for miss loses its final letter

parts.note: to miss out on something is to lose it
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper; the 's stands for is and joins

explanation.surface: A young woman is spotted near a police officer's station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a young woman and 'copper' like a police officer. 'mostly' cuts LOSE to LOS, and 'seen round' puts it around CU, copper's chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A locus is a precise position or site, a formal synonym for a place.

clue.text: Digital recording of case by actors

parts.note: a pod is the case holding peas or seeds
the cast is the set of actors in a production

explanation.surface: Someone describes an audio file of a court case made by a troupe of performers.
explanation.definitionFit: A downloadable audio or video series episode is a kind of digital recording.

clue.text: Slip up in attempt to produce a fortified wine

indicators.note: in places the mistake inside the word for an attempt

parts.note: a shy is a throw or try, as at a coconut shy
to err is to slip up or make a mistake

explanation.surface: A clumsy effort at winemaking turns out a fortified wine after all.
explanation.walkthrough: A shy is an attempt, as at a fairground coconut shy, where people throw balls at coconuts.
explanation.definitionFit: This Spanish wine from Jerez, strengthened with brandy, is a classic example of a fortified wine.

clue.text: Street guide (centre of Doncaster) in pub in marketplace

indicators.note: in tells us the guide and letter go inside the pub word

parts.note: a bar is a pub or the counter in one
the A-Z is the classic British book of street maps

indicators.note: centre of picks the middle letter of the word Doncaster

explanation.surface: Someone consults a street map in a Doncaster pub while looking for the market.
explanation.walkthrough: The A-Z is a British street atlas, written AZ here. 'centre of' takes A, the middle letter of 'Doncaster' (a town in Yorkshire), and both go 'in' BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A bazaar is an oriental market or a fund-raising sale, a type of marketplace.

clue.text: Lecture a daughter in connection with clothes

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter, as in genealogies
dress means clothing, as in formal dress

explanation.surface: A parent lectures their daughter about what she wears.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal talk or speech to an audience is a near-synonym of a lecture.

clue.text: Page well-informed about trendy page-three girl?

indicators.note: about means the first two pieces surround the trendy word

parts.note: to be up on a subject is to be well-informed about it
in means fashionable or trendy

explanation.surface: A page reporter knows all about the fashionable topless model.
explanation.walkthrough: A page-three girl was a glamour model pictured on page three of The Sun, a British tabloid; the question mark marks her as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A glamour model whose photo is pinned to a wall is an example, signalled by the question mark.

clue.text: Show trial

definitions.meaning: a display or exhibition of how something works
a test run, as in a product being tried out in front of buyers

explanation.surface: A political show trial, staged for propaganda.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show trial' reads as one phrase but splits into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a public display and a practical test run are senses of the same noun.

clue.text: Only minutes before

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: Just a few minutes earlier, someone says.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, 'only' and this word both mean nothing more than, as in a mere child.

clue.text: Stormy debates involving head of his chapel

indicators.note: involving means the rearranged letters take in the extra one
stormy suggests the letters of debates are thrown about
head of picks the first letter of the word his

explanation.surface: Heated arguments break out with a minister at the head of his congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stormy' rearranges DEBATES, and 'involving' puts H, the first letter of 'his' ('head of'), into it.
explanation.definitionFit: This biblical pool name was often given to Nonconformist places of worship, especially in Wales, so it names a chapel.

clue.text: Rest for artist? After rest, left

indicators.note: after places the left letter at the end, behind the word for rest

parts.note: to ease is to rest or relax

explanation.surface: A painter, after a break, goes home.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Rest' is a noun, a stand that supports a canvas; the second means to relax.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter's frame that supports a canvas is literally a stand or prop for the artist's work.

clue.text: Nothing cold and hot in cheese roll

indicators.note: in places the three single letters within the cheese word

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
O looks like zero, nothing
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A cheese roll is described as containing nothing, served either cold or hot.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'roll' looks like part of a cheese roll, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This rich French bread made with butter and eggs is often baked as a small roll or bun.

clue.text: One who can get a box, say, back into shape?

definitions.text: One who can get a box, say, back into shape?

parts.words: One who can get a box, say, back into shape?
parts.note: box is an evergreen shrub, so one who restores it is a tree specialist, not a boxer's trainer

explanation.surface: Someone who can repair a battered cardboard box, or train a boxer back to fitness.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'box' seems like a container or boxing, but box is a hedge plant pruned into shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: An arborist who prunes and treats trees and shrubs, including box, restores their form.

clue.text: Thrown into ecstasy, pet ran wild

indicators.note: wild says the letters of pet ran run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A pet animal ran about madly, overjoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' signals an anagram of PET RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Being rapt or spellbound means being carried away with delight, a literary synonym.

clue.text: A second artist lifted bouquet

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue means the whole string is read upwards

parts.note: a mo is a moment or second, as in 'half a mo'
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist quickly snatched a bunch of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns A + MO + RA upwards, as this is a down clue. 'Bouquet' is a wine's scent, not flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A bouquet is the characteristic smell of a wine, a synonym for scent.

clue.text: Jersey: rainier, reportedly, after start of September

indicators.note: after sets the sound-alike piece behind the opening letter
start of takes the first letter of September
reportedly means a word heard, spelt differently from how it sounds

parts.note: rainier weather is wetter

explanation.surface: Wrap up: it gets rainier once September begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' gives a homophone of WETTER (rainier), spelt WEATER; 'after' puts it behind S, from 'start of September'. Jersey looks like the Channel Island.
explanation.definitionFit: A jersey is a knitted pullover, a synonym of this garment.

clue.text: Maybe what a diver did gained recognition?

definitions.meaning: a diver entering water literally created a splash
to become noticed or famous suddenly

explanation.surface: A diver's spectacular entry earned them fame.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a sensational debut is taken literally for a diver hitting the water.

clue.text: Smart do organised for celebrity

indicators.note: organised suggests the letters of smart do are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A smart party was arranged for a famous person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' signals an anagram of SMART DO.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrity as a state of fame is a synonym of being a star.

clue.text: Relatives, for instance, to admit free

indicators.note: to admit means the instance word lets the freeing word in

parts.note: as means for instance, as in 'cities such as Rome'
to untie is to set free

explanation.surface: Family members, for example, are let in without charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' looks like an adjective (no charge) but is the verb, to release.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisters of one's parents are an example of relatives, family members.

clue.text: Fly, being part of jet set's entourage

indicators.note: being part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone flies off, joining the jet set's hangers-on.
explanation.definitionFit: This African bloodsucking insect that spreads sleeping sickness is a species of fly.

clue.text: Slightly reduced, modest object

indicators.note: slightly reduced means the modest word loses just its final letter

parts.note: demure means modest or reserved

explanation.surface: A small, unpretentious item has been marked down a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'object' looks like a noun, but it is the verb, to protest.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise an objection or protest is a formal synonym of the verb object.

clue.text: Mountain-dweller also described by father

indicators.note: described by means the also word is drawn around, enclosed, by the father word

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: A father describes someone else who lives in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'described by' is used in the geometric sense, as a circle is described around a shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant bear of central China lives in mountain bamboo forests, an example of a mountain-dweller.
